survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is descriptive and does not report an individual-student large-scale assessment microdata analysis (no sampling frame, no analytic subsample, and no model-based estimation that would require student or replicate weights). The figures and tables referenced (e.g., NEET rates, educational attainment, expenditure per student, instruction time, class size) are presented as system-level indicators for Brazil using the latest available reference year(s) in Education at a Glance 2025. Because no student-level PV-based achievement modeling is conducted here, complex survey weighting variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) are not applicable to the note’s reported outputs. For users who want to reproduce any underlying indicator estimates from the OECD/partner microdata, the appropriate weights would depend on the original source dataset used by Education at a Glance 2025; this note itself does not specify them.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive country note summarising education-system indicators rather than an empirical student-level analysis that would require plausible values (PVs) for cognitive achievement domains. The note does not describe any PV-based outcome variable or any statistical model for which missing-data handling would be specified. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported in the context of this note, and the absence reflects the reporting scope (indicator presentation) rather than a methodological omission for an ML/PV pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is not an ILSA microdata analysis paper; it is a descriptive OECD country note using the latest available reference-year data compiled in Education at a Glance 2025. No student-level analytic sample is defined, and no inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., grade bands, assessment modules, completion thresholds) are specified in the note.

data.outcome_summary: Education at a Glance 2025 (Brazil country note) provides a descriptive overview of education-system characteristics using the latest available reference-year data compiled in OECD’s Education at a Glance 2025 indicators. The note highlights labour-market and attainment outcomes (e.g., NEET rates for 18–24 year-olds; unemployment by educational attainment), tertiary participation and completion patterns (e.g., bachelor’s completion within theoretical duration and dropout after the first year), and system inputs (e.g., public expenditure per student by education level, instruction time, and class size). It also reports policy-relevant institutional features such as selective tertiary admissions and the use of entrance examination results for financial support. No student-level large-scale assessment (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) microdata, plausible values, or ML prediction models are estimated in this note; consequently, there are no model performance metrics or causal claims to interpret.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction corresponds to an OECD descriptive country note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis. As a result, there is no student-level dataset, no PV-based achievement outcome, no ML model training/evaluation, and no reported analytic sample size or per-country student counts. The sparse methodological fields (e.g., weights, missing-data handling, PV handling) are therefore expected given the note’s purpose: indicator presentation and system description rather than statistical modeling.
